The first layer and soil map components

Source: vignettes/first-layer.Rmd
first-layer.Rmd
library(soilhub)

Many studies need only the topsoil: the first horizon of each profile. This guide shows how to ask for it with layer = "first", how to read the column first_layer_status, and how the soil map units of SOTER and SOTWIS are split into components. It assumes you have signed in as shown in vignette("soilhub", package = "soilhub"). The outputs were recorded from the Global Soil Data Hub API in October 2026.

The first layer of each profile

With layer = "first" the hub returns, for each profile, only its first horizon (or horizons, when several start at the same depth). Here: the WoSIS profiles around Vancouver (Canada).

vancouver <- c(-123.3, 49.0, -122.9, 49.4)
first <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", bbox = vancouver,
                           layer = "first", max_rows = 5)
nrow(first)
#> [1] 3

We asked for up to 5 rows and received 3: one row per profile, and there are only three profiles with horizons in this box.

first[, c("feature_id", "horizon_name", "upper_depth_cm", "lower_depth_cm", "first_layer_status")]
#> # soilhub wide table: 3 horizons, 3 features, 6 variables | wosis_points | view raw, layer first
#> # no API warnings (soil_warnings), typing (soil_columns), cite with soil_citations()
#>                             feature_id horizon_name upper_depth_cm lower_depth_cm
#> 1 38ed7f8d-35b2-4afd-b4a8-08fc5e8f4f81            F              0              1
#> 2 623b5139-52b0-40cc-9750-933440e50d57            F              0              1
#> 3 bfe48b90-466a-4741-b079-ef95b687abd7           Ap              0             20
#>   first_layer_status
#> 1            surface
#> 2            surface
#> 3            surface

Each row is the first horizon of one profile. Two profiles start with an organic F horizon (0 to 1 cm), one with a ploughed Ap horizon (0 to 20 cm). All three have the status surface.

What the status means

first_layer_status says how the first horizon was found. soil_first_layer() lists the statuses the server can give:

soil_first_layer(first)
#> $view
#> [1] "raw"
#> 
#> $statuses
#> [1] "surface"       "tie"           "not_surface"   "depth_missing"
#> 
#> $profile_markings
#> [1] "negative_depth_above"  "empty_row"             "depth_order_conflict" 
#> [4] "numbering_starts_at_N" "numbering_gap"

In words:

  • surface: the one horizon of the profile that starts at the soil surface (upper depth 0);
  • tie: several horizons start at 0; all of them are returned (for example repeated samples of the same layer);
  • not_surface: no horizon starts at the surface; the first available one is returned (look at its upper_depth_cm);
  • depth_missing: SOTER only, the surface horizon has neither an upper nor a lower depth.

With view = "revised" (see vignette("raw-vs-revised", package = "soilhub")) two more statuses can appear: surface_within_5cm (rule R2: a first horizon starting within 5 cm counts as surface) and first_mineral (rule R3: the first mineral horizon, below the organic layers).

You can count the statuses with table():

table(first$first_layer_status)
#> 
#> surface 
#>       3

Profile markings

The column profile_markings reports problems of the horizon sequence of the profile in the source (SOTER profiles only; it is empty elsewhere). The list of possible markings is in soil_first_layer(first)$profile_markings:

  • negative_depth_above: an organic (O) horizon with a negative depth lies above the first horizon;
  • empty_row: the first row of the profile is empty (no name, depth or value);
  • depth_order_conflict: some horizons are not deeper than the previous one;
  • numbering_starts_at_N: the horizon numbers (SOTER HONU) do not start at 1;
  • numbering_gap: some horizon numbers are missing.

Here the profiles are from WoSIS, so the markings are empty:

first$profile_markings
#> [[1]]
#> character(0)
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> character(0)
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> character(0)

Why a profile may return nothing

soil_features() lists the places (features) of a selection, even those without measurements. Here we read the first three features of the same box, with their coordinates as text (GeoJSON):

places <- soil_features(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", bbox = vancouver,
                        with_geometry = "text", max_rows = 3)
places[, c("feature_id", "geometry_text")]
#> # soilhub features table: 3 features | wosis_points | view raw
#> # no API warnings (soil_warnings), cite with soil_citations()
#> # incomplete read: continue with offset = 3 (soil_metadata(x)$next_offset)
#>                             feature_id
#> 1 14f7a6b1-13c0-4c75-a7fb-dbc370ae5d44
#> 2 38ed7f8d-35b2-4afd-b4a8-08fc5e8f4f81
#> 3 623b5139-52b0-40cc-9750-933440e50d57
#>                                                  geometry_text
#> 1 {"type":"Point","coordinates":[-123.152777778,49.088888889]}
#> 2                  {"type":"Point","coordinates":[-123,49.38]}
#> 3                  {"type":"Point","coordinates":[-123,49.38]}

Is each of them among the profiles of the first-layer read?

places$feature_id %in% first$feature_id
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE  TRUE

The first place has no row: it is a profile site without any horizon with measurements in WoSIS, so a read of observations (first layer or all layers) returns nothing for it. A profile can also return nothing with layer = "first" when its first horizon has no value of the variables you asked for, or, in SOTER, when its first row is empty.

Soil map units and their components

SOTER and SOTWIS describe the soil of map units (polygons). A map unit holds several soils, the components, each covering a share of its area and represented by a profile. We read five horizons of the SOTER polygons:

soter <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "soter_polygons", max_rows = 5)
soter[, c("component_rank", "proportion_percent", "is_representative", "suid",
          "horizon_name", "lower_depth_cm")]
#> # soilhub wide table: 5 horizons, 9 variables | soter_polygons | view raw, layer all
#> # no API warnings (soil_warnings), typing (soil_columns), cite with soil_citations()
#> # incomplete read: continue with offset = 5 (soil_metadata(x)$next_offset)
#>   component_rank proportion_percent is_representative suid horizon_name lower_depth_cm
#> 1              1                100              TRUE  866           Aa             12
#> 2              1                100              TRUE  866           Ap             21
#> 3              1                100              TRUE  866           W1             42
#> 4              1                100              TRUE  866           W1            100
#> 5              1                100              TRUE 1409          A11             31

The component columns:

  • component_rank: the rank of the component in the map unit (1 is the largest);
  • proportion_percent: the share of the map unit it covers (100 % here: these units have one soil);
  • is_representative: TRUE for the component that represents the unit;
  • suid: the SOTER unit identifier (SUID) of the map unit.

The upper depths of these SOTER horizons are missing in the source (upper_depth_cm is NA): only the lower depth is recorded.

soter$upper_depth_cm
#> [1] NA NA NA NA NA

Which components were returned? By default only the representative one:

soil_metadata(soter)$components
#> [1] "representative"

Choosing the components

The argument components chooses which components you get:

  • "representative": one component per map unit, the representative one;
  • "all": every component;
  • "cumulative": the largest components until their shares add up to min_cumulative_percent.

A SOTWIS example near Tunis

SOTWIS map units have several soil components. We look at three SOTWIS map units in a box near Tunis (Tunisia). First, the box:

tunis <- c(10.0, 36.5, 10.5, 37.0)

soil_features() lists the map units without reading their horizons (here with the shapes as text; with_geometry = "sf", the default, returns them as an sf object for maps if the package sf is installed):

units <- soil_features(soil, datasets = "sotwis_polygons", bbox = tunis,
                       with_geometry = "text", max_rows = 3, progress = FALSE)
nrow(units)
#> [1] 3

Each of the three rows is one SOTWIS map unit (a polygon). The column components holds, for each unit, a small table with its soil components; here is the one of the first unit:

units$components[[1]][, c("soil_code", "component_rank", "proportion_percent",
                          "is_representative")]
#>   soil_code component_rank proportion_percent is_representative
#> 1       GLe              1                 55              TRUE

The first unit has a Gleysol (GLe) component covering 55 % of the unit; it is the largest (component_rank 1) and represents the unit. Its horizons are read with soil_observations(), asking for all the components (components = "all"):

sotwis <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "sotwis_polygons", bbox = tunis,
                            components = "all", max_rows = 5, progress = FALSE)
sotwis[, c("component_rank", "proportion_percent", "horizon_name",
           "upper_depth_cm", "lower_depth_cm")]
#> # soilhub wide table: 5 horizons, 18 variables | sotwis_polygons | view raw, layer all
#> # no API warnings (soil_warnings), typing (soil_columns), cite with soil_citations()
#> # incomplete read: continue with offset = 5 (soil_metadata(x)$next_offset)
#>   component_rank proportion_percent horizon_name upper_depth_cm lower_depth_cm
#> 1              1                 55           D1              0             20
#> 2              1                 55           D1              0             20
#> 3              1                 55           D2             20             40
#> 4              1                 55           D3             40             60
#> 5              1                 55           D4             60             80

These five rows are the horizons of the first component, from 0 to 80 cm. We stopped at 5 rows, so the other components of the unit are not shown: raise max_rows to read them. The first horizon, D1, is listed twice with the same values: the SOTWIS files of ISRIC carry a summary copy of the first layer, and the hub keeps the source as ISRIC published it. With view = "revised" the copy is hidden (rule R5, see the article on the raw and revised views).

A few values of those horizons (SOTWIS values are estimates, not measurements):

sotwis[, c("horizon_name", "clay_content", "organic_carbon", "ph_h2o")]
#> # soilhub wide table: 5 horizons, 18 variables | sotwis_polygons | view raw, layer all
#> # no API warnings (soil_warnings), typing (soil_columns), cite with soil_citations()
#> # incomplete read: continue with offset = 5 (soil_metadata(x)$next_offset)
#>   horizon_name clay_content organic_carbon ph_h2o
#> 1           D1           30          10.00    5.9
#> 2           D1           30          10.00    5.9
#> 3           D2           34           4.34    6.0
#> 4           D3           34           3.75    6.2
#> 5           D4           34           3.00    6.4

For a soil scientist: a SOTWIS polygon is a map unit made of several soil components, each with a share of the area in percent, and the layers of a component are estimated values for the representative soil, not measurements of a profile at a site (source_support is "polygon_estimate"). Here clay is 30 to 34 %, organic carbon decreases with depth (from 10 to 3 g/kg) and the pH rises from 5.9 to 6.4.

Other components

For example, all the components of the SOTWIS map units of Kenya, or the largest ones covering at least 80 % of each unit (these calls are not run here):

all_components <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "sotwis_components",
                                    country = "KEN", components = "all")

main_components <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "sotwis_components",
                                     country = "KEN", components = "cumulative",
                                     min_cumulative_percent = 80)

You can combine components with layer = "first" to get the topsoil of each component.
